key_insight: In a report-conditioned medical VLM, having the radiology report available made the model much less likely to change its answer when the image was swapped, suggesting reduced dependence on visual input under this protocol.
clinical_relevance: This matters because it flags a potential risk that some report-conditioned radiology AI systems may lean on text context more than the image, which could affect how reliably they are used or evaluated in imaging workflows.
method: Paired image-swap audit on 3,199 MIMIC-CXR cases from 293 patients.
Each case had 14 questions: 13 finding-specific plus 1 composite.
Compared model answer changes with the report present vs absent while keeping question and report fixed.
evidence_signal: MedGemma-27B changed its generated answer in 4.26% of trials with the report versus 20.94% without it, a paired increase of 16.7 points (patient-clustered 95% CI 15.6 to 17.7).
watch_item: Because the labels were derived from radiology reports, the study measures sensitivity to image swaps rather than direct visual correctness, so results should not be interpreted as proof of image understanding quality.
paper_title: ModaLens: Measuring Image Sensitivity in Report-Conditioned Medical VLMs
